title: Meta's Joel Kaplan Apologizes to India Over Restricted Modi Facebook Post
excerpt: Meta's Chief Global Affairs Officer personally apologized to India's IT minister for briefly blocking PM Modi's video, as tensions escalate between the government and the tech giant over content moderation and platform accountability.
body:
• Meta's Chief Global Affairs Officer Joel Kaplan personally apologized to India's IT minister for restricting PM Modi's Facebook post in July, calling it an operational error.
  • India's IT ministry said Meta's explanation was "not reasonable" and the matter is "not settled," signaling continued regulatory pressure.
  • Police in Hyderabad filed a case against Meta India head Arun Srinivas over videos allegedly depicting Modi in an abusive manner during student protests.
  • Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg separately apologized to the Indian government over child sexual abuse material, deepfake content, and other operational lapses on its platforms.

Meta Platforms' Chief Global Affairs Officer Joel Kaplan apologized to India's information technology minister on Wednesday for briefly restricting a post by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in July, escalating a confrontation between the world's largest social media company and its biggest market by users.

The Apology

"I apologized to the minister on behalf of Meta for the error restricting PM Modi's post," Kaplan said in a statement. The apology follows weeks of mounting pressure after Facebook temporarily blocked a video posted by Modi on July 23 — his first direct address to young people amid the largest wave of student protests India has seen in more than a decade.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=r16r5hqXEpI

The video, originally posted on Instagram where it gathered more than 404 million views, was shared to Facebook and then briefly restricted in the early hours of July 28. Meta said the post was blocked inadvertently because of an automated content filtering error and restored it the same day.

India Rejects the Explanation

The Indian government has not accepted Meta's characterization of the incident as a simple technical glitch. IT Ministry Secretary S. Krishnan summoned Meta executives to explain the matter "at the highest level" after the restriction came to light.

"Meta's explanation is not reasonable, and deeper discussions are needed. The matter is not settled and done."

— Government sources, per PTI

Officials argued that a technical error alone could not adequately explain why the official account of a sitting prime minister was affected. The government expects Meta to strengthen its automated moderation tools and ensure similar incidents do not recur.

Wider Tensions

The post restriction is part of a broader run of confrontations between Meta and Modi's government. Police in Hyderabad registered a case against Meta India managing director Arun Srinivas over videos posted on Facebook that allegedly depicted Modi in an abusive manner, Reuters reported. The videos spread during weeks of youth-led protests triggered by leaked examination papers, which led to the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

BJP members criticized Meta's actions publicly. Priti Gandhi, a party worker, questioned the platform's transparency on X: "The Prime Minister of the world's largest democracy uploads his first direct selfie video to connect with India's youth... and Facebook restricts it? Who gave Meta the authority to decide what millions of Indians should or should not see?"

Zuckerberg's Separate Apology

In a separate development on the same day, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg apologized to the Indian government over child sexual abuse material, deepfake content, and other operational lapses on Meta's platforms, according to Moneycontrol and other local outlets. The apology came during a meeting between Meta executives and Indian government officials.

In July, the government ordered Meta to remove advertisements and content promoting child sexual abuse material on Instagram, according to the BBC. Meta said at the time it maintains a zero-tolerance policy on such material and was continuing to strengthen its detection systems.

The Stakes

India is Facebook's largest market by users, making the regulatory relationship critical for Meta's global business. The government's willingness to summon executives, reject technical explanations, and pursue criminal cases signals an approach to platform accountability that goes well beyond the content moderation debates playing out in the United States and Europe.

For Meta, resolving the tension requires more than apologies. The government has made clear it expects systemic changes to how automated moderation handles content from constitutional authorities — a standard that, if formalized, could reshape how global tech platforms operate in India.
nri_angle: The standoff highlights the regulatory environment Indian-origin tech executives navigate at global platforms, and raises questions about how content moderation systems handle political speech in the world's largest democracy.
